cards.summary: 特朗普拒绝了伊朗提出的在七天内重新开放霍尔木兹海峡的协议方案。伊朗外长确认已注意到特朗普的表态，但表示德黑兰仍在等待调解方的最终意见。此举意味着美伊围绕这一关键石油通道的紧张对峙短期内难以缓解。
cards.relevant: 霍尔木兹海峡是全球能源命脉，任何封锁或冲突都会直接冲击国际油价和全球供应链。
cards.context: 此前美伊关系持续紧张，霍尔木兹海峡的通航安全成为双方博弈焦点。伊朗提出以七天为期限重开海峡的协议，但特朗普明确拒绝，伊朗则等待中间调解方的进一步表态。
cards.source_analysis: BBC报道，立场相对中立，以事实陈述为主。
cards.social_impact: 霍尔木兹海峡若持续受阻，将影响全球约20%的石油运输量，可能推高国际油价并加剧全球通胀压力。
cards.source_text: Trump rejects Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days - Published US President Donald Trump has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping within a week. He told reporters at the White House that Tehran "want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they're losing so badly". In a post on Telegram, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi acknowledged Trump's comments, but said Tehran would wait for an official response from mediators. On Friday, Araghchi had told reporters at the UN in New York that an agreement could be reached "if the necessary conditions are met" and that these were contained in a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed by the two countries in June. The vital waterway through which around a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows has been effectively closed since the outbreak of war in February. "I'm rejecting their deal," Trump said on Saturday, adding that the US already had "total control" of the strait, with "massive amounts of oil" passing through it. "They want to make a deal, and I think that's fine. I like making a deal, too. But that deal would not be acceptable," he added. Araghchi wrote that Trump "has made many good statements, as well as many contradictory ones, which unfortunately we hear frequently." He added that he would await the "definitive views" of mediators, and that Tehran "will make a decision based on that." On Friday the Wall Street Journal, external cited officials as saying Trump was sceptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he saw a renewed bombing campaign as probable. Iran responded to US and Israeli air strikes, beginning in late February, by attacking Israel and US bases in the Gulf and Arab Gulf allies of the US - as well as blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Its closure has caused wild fluctuations of energy prices. The economic effects have also increased pressure on Trump to find a way of ending the conflict - particularly as the US heads towards Congressional elections in November. Araghchi told reporters on Friday: "If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, a normal maritime passage restored within seven days," He added that "the actions that the United States should take are not new. They are all already in the MOU... The choice now rests with the United States." Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, told CBS News, the BBC's US partner: "We had previously r
cards.source_title: Trump rejects Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days

cards.relevant: 埃塞俄比亚是非洲人口第二大国，若再次陷入内战将引发严重的人道主义危机和地区动荡。

cards.social_impact: 前次内战已致约60万人死亡，若冲突全面重启，将波及数百万平民，并可能引发大规模难民潮涌向邻国。
cards.source_text: There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed. About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict. On Sunday, seven armed groups from around the country, including the TPLF, announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, aimed at deposing the government in Addis Ababa. Then, on Wednesday, the TPLF seized control of three airports from federal police. The state-owned carrier, Ethiopian Airlines, said it had suspended flights to the region “due to the current situation”. The TPLF also launched attacks into Afar and Amhara. A humanitarian source in Afar told Agence France-Presse there were heavy artillery attacks by the group on Thursday as they attempted to take control of the town of Yallo, near the Tigrayan border. Flights to the historic Ethiopian town of Lalibela were also suspended on Thursday because of nearby fighting, while people in Tigray stocked up on food and cash, with one resident telling Reuters that people there feared they could face siege conditions similar to those during the previous war. A resident of Adigrat, a city close to the Eritrean border, described panic-buying and shops emptying. “Food shortages are worsening as market shelves sit empty … Essential medicines remain scarce and astronomically expensive,” he told Reuters. “Daily survival has become a constant calculation.” The TPLF’s vice-president, Amanuel Assefa, told AFP: “We are in the situation of full-blown war now.” He confirmed Tigrayan forces were fighting alongside local armed groups in Afar and Amhara. The group took control of Abala, also on the Tigray-Afar border, on Wednesday, a foreign security source based in Ethiopia told AFP, while a TPLF source said they had seized several other towns in Afar. The foreign security source also said there was fighting around the Amhara town of Weldiya – one of the few routes to the capital. cards.source_title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war

cards.relevant: 伦敦作为全球金融中心的地位近年受到严重挑战，此次大型IPO被视为对英国资本市场信心的重要测试。

cards.social_impact: Airtel Money业务覆盖多个非洲国家，上市后预计估值达90亿美元，将成为近年来伦敦最大IPO之一。
cards.source_text: A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange. Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures. The company is understood to be hoping to raise about $800m (£601m) from the initial public offering (IPO) and is targeting a valuation of $8bn to $9bn, which would make it one of London’s largest listings in recent years. Airtel Money has 53 million monthly active users across 13 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, including Uganda, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo. It operates through a network of branches and kiosks, which enable customers to load money on to their phones, withdraw cash and access other money services, and the company generated revenues of just under $1.4bn in the last financial year. Airtel Money’s parent company is Airtel Africa, a telecoms provider that is part of the Indian conglomerate Bharti Enterprises, which is ultimately controlled by the billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal. Airtel Africa is already listed on the FTSE 100 but said it wanted Airtel Money to be listed separately. “From a company perspective, [the listing] gives us flexibility for the future,” said Airtel Money’s chief executive, Ian Ferrao. “We evaluated multiple [stock] exchanges, including the Middle East because we’ve got a headquarters in Dubai, along with European and North American exchanges. Ultimately, shareholders felt that London was the right choice. We still believe there is deep capital available … all the global institutional investors are here.” Ferrao added: “Most importantly there’s a deep understanding of emerging markets in the London market and Africa specifically.” Airtel Money said it would announce more details about the float in early October, including the indicative price range and number of shares to be offered, with final pricing to follow later in the month. Airtel Africa had originally targeted a listing in the first six months of 2026 but delayed it to the second half of the year, blaming unfavourable market conditions as a result of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Several other companies also pushed back planned IPOs amid the market volatility caused by the conflict. Airtel Africa owns just under 78% of Airtel Money and will remain a long-term investor after the I
cards.source_title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years

cards.source_analysis: 《卫报》报道，立场偏自由派，关注人道主义和发展议题。

cards.source_text: The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put healthcare in Africa and the global south “under growing strain” a new report warns. The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region. The report, titled A Sovereign Future For Health, was created by the Accra Reset, a global health initiative led by John Dramani Mahama, Ghana’s president, that believes countries in Africa and the wider global south should have greater control over their health development rather than being dependent on aid from western countries and international institutions. A key statistic cited by Mahama and Accra Reset is that Africa produces less than 1% of its vaccines while carrying about 25% of the global disease burden. The report cites how abrupt changes to global health financing, such as the US withdrawal from several global health initiatives, forced countries within the global south to urgently restructure their finances. The report points to the Trump administration’s decision to dissolve USAID, which pushed Nigeria to absorb the 28,000 health workers who were previously employed by the agency at a cost of $200m. External financing for health in Africa contracted by close to 70% between 2021 and 2025, the report notes, meaning that African countries historically dependent on aid were forced to adapt quickly. The withdrawal of the US Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar) funding for South Africa, which provided over $400m a year annually and is credited with saving 26m lives globally since 2003, led to HIV clinics closing across the country. That left 1.4 million people living with HIV to face uncertainty about their treatment. Such funding cuts caused “severe and devastating” disruption globally, according to research presented at the 26th International Aids Conference in Brazil earlier this year. At the World Health Assembly in May, Mahama said Ghana lost $78m after the closure of USAID programs which affected maternal healthcare, the treatment of malaria, nutrition and HIV/Aids interventions. The initiative’s latest report, published on Monday, comes amid these major cuts to international aid and growing pressure on countries to take greater ownership of their health systems. cards.source_title: Healthcare in Africa ‘under growing strain’ after US withdrawal from aid programs, report warns

cards.source_text: MOSCOW, September 26. /TASS/. Russia and Germany could jointly restart the Nord Stream gas pipeline that was sabotaged four years ago, special presidential envoy and Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) CEO Kirill Dmitriev argued. "All true. Jointly we will reopen Nord Stream. AfD is the voice of German people that fights for German energy sovereignty, prosperity, peace and cooperation," he wrote in an English-language post on X. Dmitriev was commenting on a remark on the same social media platform from Tino Chrupalla, co-chairman of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, who proposed conducting an international probe into the sabotage on Nord Stream and Nord Stream 2 pipelines as he also insisted that the two pipelines be repaired and reopened. On September 26, 2022, unprecedented damage was recorded on three strings of the Nord Stream pipelines and the never-commissioned Nord Stream 2 pipeline. The Russian Prosecutor General’s Office opened a criminal case over an act of international terrorism.
cards.source_title: Putin’s envoy says Russia, Germany could reopen Nord Stream jointly

cards.source_text: BEIRUT, September 27. /TASS/. The death toll from Israeli army strikes on the Gaza Strip over the past 48 hours has reached seven, with another 38 people wounded, according to a report by the Palestinian enclave's Health Ministry posted on the X social media platform. According to the ministry, the bodies of seven killed residents were brought to Gaza hospitals, and medical aid was provided to 38 wounded individuals, including women and children. Most of the victims were brought from the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood and the Nuseirat refugee camp, where Israeli forces had been conducting intense fire. Since the start of the truce on October 11, 2025, 1,415 people have been killed and another 4,953 wounded during Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling, the ministry said. The total death toll from the escalation of the conflict in Gaza since October 2023 has risen to 74,016, with the number of injured reaching 175,068, the ministry added.
cards.source_title: Seven Palestinians killed in Gaza Strip during Israeli attacks — Health Ministry

cards.source_analysis: TASS（塔斯社）为俄罗斯官方通讯社，报道侧重军事行动细节，立场倾向批评以色列。
cards.source_text: BEIRUT, September 27. /TASS/. Israeli Air Force fighter jets resumed attacks on Saturday against mountainous areas near the Lebanese towns of Jezzine and Nabatieh, located north of the Litani River. According to the Janoubia news portal, intense airstrikes targeted underground shelters, command posts, and depots belonging to the Shiite organization Hezbollah on the heights of Jebel al-Rafi, Rayhan, and Sajoud. The portal reports that the resistance forces' largest outpost in this southern region is situated in the mountainous Iqlim al-Tuffah area. Following the destruction of Hezbollah's underground infrastructure on the Ali al-Taher heights on September 10, the Israeli command intends to focus its strikes on this sector. Ground operations are expected to follow the massive bombardment of Iqlim al-Tuffah. Currently, ahead of a new escalation in hostilities, a rotation of Israeli forces stationed in the buffer zone in southern Lebanon is underway. According to the portal, powerful explosions rocked the towns of Majdal Zoun and Mays al-Jabal on Saturday afternoon as they came under Israeli artillery fire. Artillery shells also struck the town of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah. Local authorities reported damage to residential homes and other structures, but no casualties were reported.
cards.source_title: Israeli aircraft launch series of strikes on mountainous areas in southern Lebanon

cards.source_text: Nika’s story No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out. Their destination was Central African Republic (CAR), a country few of them had even heard of. Nika, a 32-year-old Iranian woman, recalled how the handcuffs dug into her wrists. She begged the officers to loosen them, but they did not. Other passengers had it worse, she said. Some of the men were restrained in black and yellow body wraps, as if mummified, after resisting orders to get on the plane. Nika, who had fled Iran 18 months earlier after protesting against its regime, had imagined the US as a place of sanctuary. Iran was already one of the most repressive countries in the world when she left, and its horrors had only deepened since then: security forces gunned down thousands of other demonstrators this year, then Donald Trump’s administration launched the war there. After more than a year locked up in a US immigration detention centre, Nika, whose name the Guardian has changed to protect her family in Iran, was granted legal protections and freed on a judge’s orders. Within two weeks, the Department of Homeland Security had rearrested her, and days later she was on the plane heading 7,000 miles east. “They never told me they were going to deport me [to] this country,” she told the Guardian. “I don’t know anything about Africa.” The Department of State warns US citizens not to travel to CAR because it says it is too dangerous. Nika spends most of her days there under a form of self-imprisonment, too scared to venture out from her small bedroom as she waits for an answer to the question on which her life depends: will she be sent back to Iran, and to a regime that could kill her? Nika is one of more than 25,000 people deported by the Trump administration to countries that are not their own. About 20,000 people have been bussed to Mexico, according to a count by Refugees International and Human Rights First. And more than 5,000 others have been put on flights to countries in Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean and central Asia to which they have no connection, and then, often, returned to the countries where US immigration judges had ruled their lives or liberty were at risk. cards.source_text: British national among six dead in building explosion close to Acropolis in Athens - Published Six people have died, including a British national, in an explosion that destroyed a building containing a holiday rental property in the historic centre of Athens. The blast on Friday happened in the Plaka area of the Greek capital, a neighbourhood close to tourist sites such as the Acropolis. Four American holidaymakers were among the dead, along with a UK national and Greek national - reportedly an elderly couple who lived in the same building. Pictures from the scene on Saturday showed emergency service workers searching through rubble, with a gas leak the suspected cause of the blast. All six bodies had been recovered by Saturday afternoon. Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said: "We are talking about an incredible disaster." The tourists were confirmed to be missing when they did not arrive for their flight at Athens airport later on Friday, news agency Reuters reported citing local police. The three-storey building completely collapsed due to the force of the blast, with neighbouring buildings damaged and debris scattered across the road. Local media reported people were injured by material scattered across nearby streets and some buildings needed to be evacuated. Excavators and thermal imaging cameras have been used at the scene to search for survivors. The explosion happened on a small road situated between two of Athens' most visited sites - the Acropolis and the Temple of Olympian Zeus. A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: "We are aware of a suspected explosion in Athens and are in touch with the local authorities." Get in touch Are you in the area? cards.source_text: Nor'easter brings flooding as New York and New Jersey declare emergency - Published Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm bringing coastal flooding, power cuts, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events. The so-called nor'easter is bringing "dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston on Saturday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said. States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, both of which faced a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine. Ed Sheeran's much-awaited Boston concert was among events called off due to the weather. The nor'easter caused widespread power cuts. More than 100,000 households, nearly all in the northeast US, have lost electricity, according to tracker PowerOutage. The Federal Aviation Administration recommended air passengers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 2,400 flights have been delayed and another 1,199 grounded, according to FlightAware. Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal flooding. Streets and homes were inundated with floodwater in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan on Saturday. "I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said. NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses." In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power lines. "Don't travel if you don't have to," NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater." In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved the last game in their series against the Chicago Cubs to Sunday afternoon in Florida. A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled. Nor is the Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, going ahead. Sheeran's concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said. Related topics - Published1 day ago
cards.source_title: Nor'easter brings flooding as New York and New Jersey declare emergency

cards.source_text: Pope Leo XIV celebrates open-air Mass in front of 800,000 people in central Paris More than 800,000 people filled the streets of central Paris to hear Pope Leo XIV say Mass on Saturday, according to Vatican estimates. The pontiff rounded out the second day of his four-day apostolic visit to France by praying at the Grotto of Massabielle in Lourdes, a renowned pilgrimage site for Catholics from across the world. To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement. One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site. Pope Leo XIV on Saturday rode along the Champs-Élysées in the "popemobile" and celebrated an open-air Mass in front of hundreds of thousands in Paris, before flying to the holy pilgrimage site of Lourdes in southern France. The leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics is on a four-day trip to France, an officially secular country with deep Catholic roots, on the first official papal visit there in nearly two decades. In the highlight of the visit's second day, the 71-year-old pope led believers in a Mass at Place de la Concorde, where a giant white canopy had been erected to serve as a makeshift altar. "It is truly good and pleasant when brothers and sisters come together and glorify the greatness of God," said Pope Leo, dressed in white liturgical vestments. Read more'A once-in-a-lifetime event': Faithful and curious flock to Pope Leo XIV's Mass in Paris Over more than two kilometres, some 800,000 people had gathered all the way beyond the Arc de Triomphe, the Vatican said. The city centre was sealed off for the service, with helicopters circling overhead and snipers positioned on rooftops. "It's one time in history to see the pope," said Aline Riziki, 41, who was born in the Democratic Republic of Congo and who has lived in France for 11 years. "I dropped everything to come here and see him, to pray for peace in the east" of her homeland, wracked by conflict for decades, she said. 'We're sharing this with her' Jeanne de Montagnac, 29, came with her husband and two-year-old girl, who was perched on his shoulders. "We're happy that, even if she won't remember it, we're sharing this with her," she said, a small golden cross dangling over her jumper. "It's an important moment for us to be surrounded by other people who also have faith." The first US pontiff was visiting France seven months before voters

cards.summary: 据BBC报道，约70万人聚集在巴黎市中心参加教皇利奥十四世主持的露天弥撒。教皇在活动中赞扬了年轻人的'活力与奉献精神'，并向在场信众发表讲话和祈祷。
cards.relevant: 不同媒体对同一事件的参与人数报道存在差异（BBC称70万，梵蒂冈称80万），反映大型集会人数统计的复杂性。
cards.context: 教皇利奥十四世正在对法国进行使徒访问，巴黎露天弥撒是此次访问的重要公开活动，吸引了大量天主教信徒和公众参与。
cards.source_analysis: BBC是英国公共广播机构，报道风格相对中立，此处引用的是约70万人的估计数字，与梵蒂冈官方估计的80万略有出入。
cards.social_impact: 约70万人参加的大型宗教集会，是巴黎近年来规模最大的公共活动之一，对城市安保和交通管理构成重大挑战。
cards.source_text: Pope praises young people's 'energy and commitment' at huge open-air Mass in Paris - Published Pope Leo XIV has praised the "enthusiasm, energy and commitment" young people bring to the Catholic Church as dense crowds attended an open-air Mass in Paris. An estimated 700,000 people had gathered for the Mass celebrated by the Pope from a special altar on the Place de la Concorde, on the second day of his four-day visit to France. It began after the pontiff rode down the Champs-Élysées Avenue waving to crowds from his open-topped popemobile. Many senior politicians attended the Mass. On Friday, the Pope met French President Emmanuel Macron. During Saturday's Mass, the Pope told worshippers that Catholics should not keep their faith to themselves but "let it overflow so that those you meet may be refreshed". The leader of the Catholic Church also addressed young people in his speech, describing them as "today's Church". "How beautiful it is to see your enthusiasm, energy and commitment, and the joy you bring to Christian communities," he said. After being welcomed by Macron on Friday, the Pope was joined by 80,000 young people at the Stade de France in northern Paris. Macron did not attend Saturday's event and will not be at any of the Pope's Masses during his visit, largely to avoid appearing to breach France's strict rules on the separation of Church and state. But the Mass was attended by Macron's wife Brigitte and French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. Several candidates for next year's presidential election also attended. Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally party and conservative Bruno Retailleau were both pictured at the Place de la Concorde ahead of the event, while centrists Édouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal were also spotted. Earlier on Saturday, the Pope met migrants and volunteers as he visited the Maison Bakhita centre, an association supporting refugees, and praised the organisation for inviting "us to see those who are invisible". He also stressed the "fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love". The Pope issued a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of his visit to France on Friday. Leo cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the Élysée Palace. cards.relevant: 教皇主动向青年群体示好，反映天主教会面对年轻信徒流失问题时的应对策略，试图通过青年参与来振兴教会。
